mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand but a nascent housing recovery, which historically precedes a mild equity rally over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically greater than the market median at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.0% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals persistent supply-side weakness, which historically precedes negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically less than zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5 percentage point over two months signals a disinflationary easing cycle, which typically supports equity valuations via lower inflation risk premium, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS change < -0.5% AND CPIAUCSL change < -0.5% over 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically greater than zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in real retail sales (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically greater than zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which typically boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically greater than zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) below their respective 6-month averages signals broad-based supply contraction, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 6-month MA AND HOUST < 6-month MA for current month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically less than zero at 90% confidence.
